Ambrook helps American family-run businesses become more profitable and resilient.
From volatile markets to climate shifts, independent operators face mounting pressure. While sustainable investments often yield the best long-term returns, they require financial clarity and capital that fragmented legacy systems can’t provide.

We are rebuilding the financial infrastructure that real economy operators rely on. By replacing paperwork with modern tools for accounting, banking, and spending, Ambrook gives owners the data they need to prove viability to lenders and the next generation. We empower the stewards of land and labor to make confident investments in their future.

We’re a Series B startup backed by Lachy Groom, Thrive Capital, Dylan Field, Thomson Reuters Ventures, Cameron Ventures, and leaders at Notion, Gusto, and Vercel. We’re looking for team members to help us untangle the intersection of American industry, climate, and the economy.



The Opportunity

This posting is for the spring co-op cycle, for at least 6 months from January through June 2027.

As part of our engineering co-op program, you'll work as a valued member of our team building features that directly impact farmers across America. This is an exciting opportunity to gain real-world development experience while contributing to sustainable agriculture, with mentorship from experienced engineers who are invested in your growth.

You'll also get real reps with modern AI dev tooling and with building AI products themselves. We've used AI dev tools since the earliest days of the company and stay close to the bleeding edge. Through Ambrook Labs, we're exploring AI-native features like natural language invoice drafting, voice-driven bookkeeping entry, and Desk, a task inbox that turns unstructured voice and text into organized workflows. We also speak regularly about the impact AI is having on us as people and developers, and balance marvel & enthusiasm about these tools with a respect for our craft.



We’re looking for someone who we can count on to…

 - Own: Build and ship real product features that customers use, while helping improve our infrastructure alongside experienced engineers.

 - Learn: Gain experience in engineering best practices, agile development, and working across teams while discovering how agtech and climate solutions help farmers succeed.

 - Grow: Understand the basics of agricultural finance, farm operations, and sustainability practices through hands-on project work, including how real-world financial data actually looks and how AI can help make sense of it.

 - Contribute: Help identify ways to improve our development process and codebase while learning full-stack development.



Within the first few weeks you’ll

 - Learn how to use Ambrook’s tech stack to deliver a standalone feature to our customers

 - Contribute to Engineering team meetings and review code from peers. 

 - Analyze Ambrook’s use of best practices and share a technical note with our team about where we have opportunities to improve.



By the end of your co-op you’ll…

 - Collaborate with the team on core product work.

 - Own a project from start to finish - from a technical design document through implementation. As the engineering owner, you’ll break down your project into granular pieces and practice good project management hygiene, triaging and prioritizing new issues that come in.

 - Collaborate with our Product team to influence prioritization of feature ideas and requests with insights from our audience.

 - Embed yourself deeply in understanding the state of farm finance, building a strong intuition about customer needs and audience segmentation.



About you

 - Currently pursuing B.S. (or higher) in Computer Science or a related field. Expected graduation: Spring 2028.

 - Available to work full-time in our NYC office for the spring co-op cycle, for at least 6 months from January through June 2027.

 - Excited to build software that makes natural resource industries like agriculture more sustainable and profitable.

 - Comfortable taking on ambiguous problems and creating elegant technical solutions.

 - Exhibit strong computer science fundamentals and an eagerness to learn.

 - Know when AI coding tools can expedite your workflows, and also when you need to dive into the code yourself.

 - Experience with TypeScript, React, React Native, and/or Next.js.

 - Bonus: Experience with LLM APIs, prompt engineering, or basic ML tooling.

 - Bonus: Experience in agriculture.



Our tech stack

 - Next.js / React application written in TypeScript

 - Hosted on Google Cloud

 - Firestore & Postgres & Google Cloud Storage for data storage

 - BigQuery & Data Studio for data insights



What makes this co-op special

 - Make a real difference: Build features that help farmers adopt sustainable practices and grow their businesses.

 - Experience life at a high-growth startup: See the complete product development cycle from design to deployment in a fast-paced environment.

 - Get personalized mentorship: Work directly with senior engineers who are invested in your growth.

 - Join a mission-driven team: Experience startup culture while helping build the future of sustainable agriculture.

 - Work closely with customers: Your work will help real farms and agribusinesses across America succeed - and you'll get to meet some of them.



Values

 - Real Talk – We create space for ourselves and others to be straightforward, vulnerable, and accountable.

 - Reach Understanding – We are driven by curiosity and empathy to learn about our customers, team, and world.

 - Be Proactively Resourceful – We are internally motivated and externally empowered to identify opportunities and solve problems.

 - Derisk Thoughtfully – We lean into the biggest risks we face as a company and put in the work to address them systematically.

 - Find the Positive-Sum – We believe in creating incentive structures that align the needs of our company, our customers, and our planet. 



Ambrook is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building diversity and inclusion into our core company culture.

Ambrook can support visa sponsorship (OPT/CPT, TN, J-1) for eligible candidates.

About Us

At Armadin, we're a group of engineers, researchers, and security researchers on a mission to redefine what proactive security can do in the AI era. Cyberattacks are becoming autonomous and relentless and we believe defending against threats before they materialize is one of the most powerful ways to protect the institutions the world depends on.



We're building autonomous proactive security from the ground up, reinforcing the tradecraft of elite security practioners into purpose-built security models and agents that discover risk and remediate it before organizations are breached.



Led by Kevin Mandia, founder of Mandiant ($5.4B exit to Google), our team brings together researchers and engineers from Google, xAI, Meta, Stanford, Georgia Tech, Waterloo, Berkeley, and MIT to reinvent security for an adversary that never sleeps.



The Role

As a Software Engineer Intern on the Agent Platform team, you'll help build the orchestration and reasoning systems that let our security agents operate independently at scale — investigating, triaging, and remediating risk with the judgment of an elite red teamer. You'll ship production code alongside full-time engineers from day one, paired with a mentor invested in your growth, and see your work deployed against real adversaries rather than left in a sandbox.



We're a small, fast-moving team, so interns get real ownership: you'll work across the stack, from distributed backend systems to the evaluation harnesses that keep autonomous agents safe and reliable, and you'll partner directly with founders, researchers, and customer-facing engineers to understand the problems worth solving.

 
 

What You'll Do

 - As a Software Engineer Intern, you'll be involved throughout the product lifecycle. From design and prototyping through shipping. While paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth. Day-to-day, you will:

 - Design and build components of our agentic orchestration platform. The systems that let autonomous security agents plan, act, and self-correct.

 - Contribute production code to core services, balancing latency, cost, and reliability at scale.

 - Build evaluation and observability tooling to measure and improve non-deterministic agent behavior.

 - Pair with a dedicated mentor and collaborate with engineers, researchers, and threat-intel experts to ship features end-to-end.

 - Participate in design reviews, code reviews, and team rituals just like a full-time engineer.

 

Required

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Math, or a related technical field, with an expected graduation in 2027 or 2028.

 - Comfortable writing clean, well-tested code and picking up new languages and frameworks quickly.

 - Solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems fundamentals.

 - Prior experience with Python, Go, or with LLM/agent frameworks is a plus.

 

Nice to Have

 - Experience with data visualization or graph rendering (D3 or similar).

 - Exposure to building products that emphasize reliability and scalability.

 - Open-source contributions, hackathon projects, or independent builds that show initiative.

 

Technologies We Use 

 - Our stack centers on Python and Go for backend services, React for front-end tooling, and a mix of open-source and in-house infrastructure to orchestrate and evaluate LLM-driven agents. 

 - We care more about your ability to learn than the specific languages on your resume.

ABOUT REVEL

At Revel, we are revolutionizing the way the world’s most critical hardware is controlled—across aerospace, automotive, energy, and manufacturing sectors. Our next-generation software stack combines an intuitive command/control interface, a specialized programming language tailored for hardware control, and a high-performance runtime environment. We empower engineers to build, test, and deploy critical systems rapidly, reliably, and safely.

 


THE INTERNSHIP

As an Embedded Software Engineering Intern at Revel, you’ll work on the software that connects our high-performance runtime to the physical world.

You’ll work closely with experienced software and embedded engineers to develop systems software, integrate with hardware, and build the foundations that allow Revel to reliably control complex industrial machinery. You’ll gain hands-on experience working across the boundary between software and hardware—from communication protocols and hardware interfaces to Linux systems and low-level debugging.

This is a highly technical internship for students who want to understand what happens below the application layer and build software where performance, reliability, and correctness matter.

You’ll contribute to real engineering projects, learn from senior engineers, and develop experience with the systems programming and hardware integration challenges behind critical software.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Write and contribute to Rust code targeting Linux userspace

 - Support the integration of industrial hardware and learn to work with register maps and hardware communication protocols

 - Contribute to Hardware Abstraction Layers (HALs) that allow Revel software to interface with physical hardware

 - Develop software that communicates with sensors, actuators, controllers, and other hardware

 - Learn and use hardware debugging tools such as logic analyzers and oscilloscopes

 - Write tests and contribute to improving the reliability and quality of low-level software

 - Participate in code reviews and collaborate with experienced software and embedded engineers

 - Debug issues across software, operating systems, communication interfaces, and hardware

 - Build an understanding of how reliability and correctness become critical requirements in real-world systems

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Systems Engineering at Anduril touches every phase of program execution — from proposals through design reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR), qualification testing, and delivery — and spans disciplines including mechanical, thermal, structural, electrical, software, firmware, GNC, reliability, and manufacturing (integration and test). Design review support — Prepare supporting technical materials for an upcoming design review (SRR, PDR, or CDR) for a defined subsystem. Deliverable: review package contribution and follow-up action summary.
Test planning support — Support the development of qualification or acceptance test requirements and pass/fail criteria for a defined component, including coordination with a vendor or subsystem owner. Deliverable: test plan contribution and results summary.
Cross-disciplinary integration project — Work with engineers across two or more disciplines (e.g., mechanical and software) to support integration of a defined subsystem. Deliverable: integrated subsystem passing checkout, plus a summary of cross-team tradeoffs.
Technical briefing development — Support the development of a technical briefing or status update communicating program progress to internal stakeholders. Deliverable: reviewed briefing materials used in an actual program review.

Ability to complete an in-person, 16–24 week co-op in one of our offices in 2027.

Collegiate project team, laboratory, or prior internship experience involving hardware or software systems development.
Coursework or project exposure to qualification/acceptance testing standards or methodologies.
Familiarity with U.S. government contract structures or programs (through coursework, research, or prior exposure).
Genuine interest in defense systems and complex, multi-disciplinary engineering programs.
Coursework or project exposure to complex systems development, including tradeoffs between performance, schedule, and other competing objectives.

Project Summary
The overarching goal of this R25 application is to provide training to diverse high school and undergraduate
students who will work with supportive faculty mentors to understand how environmental chemical
exposures contribute to non-communicable diseases, and how hazard and/or exposure mitigation can
improve health. Program faculty come from a diverse range of disciplines: toxicology, endocrinology, cell and
molecular biology, veterinary and animal sciences, chemistry, epidemiology, chemical engineering, civil and
environmental engineering, and science communication. We will focus on recruiting women and individuals
from underrepresented groups to participate in this summer program, which includes three aims:
1) To involve high school age young women in introductory summer research experiences and recruit those
with an interest in participating in research projects or science communication projects. By partnering with the
local Girls Inc. organization, we will offer week-long introductory training programs for 9th grade girls from
diverse but underserved communities in Western MA. With 24-26 girls participating every year, we will use this
program to recruit 10th and 11th grade girls to participate in Aims 2 and 3.
2) To create a learning community focused on understanding how environmental chemical exposures
contribute to non-communicable diseases and develop scientific strategies to create solutions to these
challenging problems. High school and undergraduate students will work with UMass faculty to understand
how environmental chemical exposures contribute to non-communicable diseases, and how hazards and/or
exposures can be mitigated. Research will focus on one of these areas:
 • molecular and cellular models of diseases relevant to environmental chemical exposures;
 • characterizing chemical exposures and their association with human diseases;
 • understanding the effects of environmental chemicals on conditions such as cancer and metabolic
diseases;
 • creating solutions for exposures to hazardous environmental chemicals including use of green chemistry
 principles to avoid hazards entirely and pollution remediation when exposures cannot be avoided.
3) To train diverse participants in methods to communicate complex environmental health concepts in the
context of our learning community and in broader communities. High school and undergraduate students will
work to create science communication tools, aimed at educating a lay audience about one or more topic
addressed in the laboratories in Aim 2. Communication tools could include static or animated infographics,
informational videos, podcasts, or other social media tools.

This Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) site at the University of Minnesota Department of Computer Science and Engineering aims to support a diverse group of undergraduate students in human-centered research projects that leverage computer science to advance social good. The objectives of this project are to: (1) provide support for undergraduate research, especially for students that are underrepresented or have limited access at their home institutions; (2) facilitate mentorship from leading researchers in virtual reality, visualization, human-computer interaction, and human-robot interaction; (3) explicitly train students in research methods and immerse them in the culture of science, and (4) provide professional development opportunities to prepare students for graduate school and scientific careers. REU student projects will produce novel technologies, algorithms, and interaction techniques that can enrich and empower human experiences with computing systems.
To achieve these goals, the REU site will recruit at least 50% of the cohort from institutions with limited research opportunities, with a particular emphasis on supporting women, underrepresented minorities, and first generation college students. Participants will be immersed in highly collaborative research labs supervised by faculty with longstanding commitments to mentoring undergraduate researchers. To help students make the connection between computer science and advancing social good, all REU projects will be aligned with one or more of the Sustainable Development Goals established by the United Nations Foundation. Students will apply their computer science knowledge to address important societal problems such as implicit bias mitigation, addiction recovery, locating underwater trash, sorting recyclables, and motivating climate action. At the cohort level, students will participate in a program of social events, research training seminars, invited research talks, and professional development workshops scheduled throughout the summer to support their scholarly and professional growth.

The University of California, Los Angeles Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) Site will provide intensive summer research opportunities in applied and computational mathematics. Each year, the program will support twelve undergraduate participants in an eight-week research experience that explores how mathematics is used to address emerging challenges in science and technology. Through faculty mentorship and collaborative research, students will develop the analytical, computational, and communication skills needed for graduate study and STEM careers. By engaging participants in research and professional development, the program contributes to the preparation of a highly trained scientific workforce and broadens pathways into advanced study and research careers. The summer experience will culminate in student presentations that communicate research outcomes to the broader scientific community.
Research projects will investigate mathematical and computational questions arising from rapidly developing areas such as artificial intelligence, quantum information science, biotechnology, healthcare, and the physical sciences. Instruction and mentoring will be integrated throughout the program, ensuring that participants acquire both the technical foundation and the research experience needed to contribute to future advances in science and technology. By connecting fundamental mathematics with real-world applications, the program advances undergraduate education while fostering the next generation of researchers in applied and computational mathematics. General Motors is seeking motivated, analytical students to join our Supplier Quality Internship Program for Summer 2027. This 12-week, project-based internship offers hands-on experience in supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and automotive engineering.

Review supplier manufacturing processes and quality systems.
Support root-cause analysis and corrective actions for supplier manufacturing and quality issues.
Participate in supplier visits to support root-cause analysis and verify corrective actions.

Support efforts to improve supplier quality performance through workshops, technical assistance, and quality-system development.
Collaborate with purchasing, product engineering, manufacturing, and supplier teams to address quality concerns and support project milestones.
Use analytical and problem-solving skills to identify trends, evaluate issues, and recommend practical solutions.

Mechanical Engineering Co-op Program
The Mechanical Engineering Co-op Program with nVent’s Electrical Connections (EC) Business is a structured experiential learning program that gives students the opportunity to couple their academic knowledge with practical situations in the workplace, and simultaneously allows nVent to evaluate students as potential direct-hire talent. The Program is rotational between various departments, including Product Engineering, Product Development, Manufacturing, Labs and Compliance, and Digital Media Development. It is designed to engage students in the entire engineering process from development, through testing and applications, and to production. Students are assigned rotations and projects based on their academic levels and engineering capabilities and are given opportunities to champion these projects to completion and make significant contributions to existing processes. Our candidates are hands-on problem-solvers who are analytical, creative, and highly professional. We seek confident leaders who take the initiative to drive results.
Depending on the degree and/or desired career path, co-ops will be placed into some combination of the following rotations. 
Applications Engineering: Co-ops work within a team of engineers who design and implement new products within existing product lines. Responsibilities may include: 
Performing engineering calculations to analyze product designs for functionality and specification accuracy 
Assisting with resolution of technical issues related to product design, system design, and compliance with industry standards 
Participating in site visits and working with end-user customers 
Participating and presenting in design review meetings 
Using 2D and 3D modeling software to create and maintain engineering documentation
New Product Development: Co-ops gain exposure to new product design by participating in the conceptualization and development of innovative new products or modifications to existing products. Co-ops will learn the art of balancing engineering design, functional requirements, customer needs, and aesthetic appeal. Responsibilities may include: 
Fabricating and evaluating product concepts 
Assisting in creation of detailed drawings, 3D models, schematics, specifications, installation instructions, assembly prints, and test reports 
Utilizing analytical tools including Finite Element Analysis (ABAQUS) and Matlab 
Participating in site and supplier visits 
Participating and presenting in design review meetings 
Labs and Product Approvals: Co-ops build and support test programs for EFS products. Responsibilities may include: 
Developing test plans to verify product design intent 
Supporting efforts to ensure product compliance with codes and standards 
Procuring and assembling materials, and conducting validation testing 
Designing and improving test fixturing 
Gaining hands- on experience using various prototyping equipment (3D prints, CNC, Laser cutter, etc.) 
Co-op Program Benefits:    
We value the opportunity to develop students' knowledge of our business, and offer a valuable benefits to our co-ops including -
Opportunities to work alongside company and industry leaders possessing top educational and career credentials, as well as diverse backgrounds and experiences
Rotation between several engineering departments and nVent Electrical Connections manufacturing facilities to experience the entire engineering process from development to production
Interaction and collaboration with global teams
Opportunity to practice classroom theories, and use experiences gained in the work environment to inform class choices and career goals
Competitive hourly pay for time worked at an hourly rate of $25.00.
Relocation and housing support is available for eligible candidates  
Co-ops receive paid time off, paid sick time, paid volunteer time, and paid holidays 
Co-ops who demonstrate outstanding performance may be offered a subsequent internship/co-op or full-time offer of employment with nVent  
Location:

Job Description
The PNC Chief Investment Office (CIO) Economics team provides economic forecasting, scenario design, modeling, and thought leadership across the organization. The team develops macroeconomic scenarios for CECL, CCAR, and other risk management applications, produces forecasts for internal and external stakeholders, supports strategic decision-making through economic analysis, and engages with clients through presentations and market insights. Team members work at the intersection of economics, risk management, and financial services, leveraging quantitative models and expert judgment to assess economic trends and their implications for PNC and its clients.
We are seeking PhD or master’s students in Economics, Finance, Econometrics, or related quantitative disciplines who are nearing graduation. This internship offers an opportunity to apply advanced economic and quantitative research techniques to real-world challenges in macroeconomic forecasting, scenario design, risk management, and financial markets. Successful candidates will have a strong analytical background and experience conducting empirical research using economic and financial data.
This position is based in New York City and requires full-time, in-office participation.
PNC will not provide sponsorship for employment visas or participate in STEM OPT for this position.
Job Responsibilities
As an intern, the candidate will participate in the many activities of the economics team. These include:
Conducting economic and financial research to support macroeconomic forecasting, scenario design, and market analysis.
Analyzing economic data, financial markets, and emerging trends to identify risks, opportunities, and key drivers of the outlook.
Assisting in the development and evaluation of quantitative models used for forecasting, stress testing, and risk management.
Preparing presentations, data visualizations, and written insights that communicate economic and market developments to internal stakeholders and clients.
We are looking for a candidate with the following:
Currently pursuing a master’s or PhD degree in Economics, Finance, Econometrics, or a related quantitative field, with an anticipated graduation date within the next 12 months.
Strong foundation in economic theory, econometrics, statistics, and empirical research methods, demonstrated through coursework, research, or professional experience.
Experience working with economic, financial, or large-scale datasets and applying quantitative methods to analyze complex problems.
Proficiency in analytical and programming tools such as Python, R, MATLAB, Stata, SAS, or similar platforms used for data analysis and modeling.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate quantitative findings into clear, actionable insights for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Accuracy and Attention to Detail, Analytical Thinking, Effective Communications, Flexibility and Adaptability, Information Capture, Initiative, Products and Services, Self-Directed Growth and Development

Who We Are
We are the first publicly-traded biotech or pharmaceutical company to take the form of a public benefit corporation. Our public benefit purpose is to provide a brighter future for patients through the development of novel pharmaceutical therapies; and technologies that expand the availability of transplantable organs.
United Therapeutics (Nasdaq: UTHR) seeks to travel down the corridors of indifference to develop treatments for rare, deadly diseases. We were founded in 1996 by a family seeking a cure for their daughter’s pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Today, we have six FDA-approved therapies that treat PAH, pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and neuroblastoma, a rare pediatric cancer. Our near-term pipeline seeks to develop additional therapies for PAH and pulmonary fibrosis (PF).
The cure for end-stage life-threatening diseases like PAH, PH-ILD, PF, and many others is an organ transplant, but only a small percentage of donated organs are available to address the vast need. For this reason, we are working to create manufactured organs to address the shortage of kidneys, hearts, lungs, and livers available for transplant. We believe an unlimited supply of tolerable, transplantable organs will eliminate the transplant waiting list and cure end-stage organ diseases for which transplant is not currently an option.
